verdict.rationale: Ramp publishes a live llms.txt (probe confirmed HTTP 200) whose content is written for agents. It tells them not to fetch the JavaScript-shell HTML pages and to use the plain-text guides instead. Alongside it sit per-guide .txt exports, /llms-api.txt, /llms-full.txt and a parseable OpenAPI spec (174 paths, probe-verified), plus an unauthenticated Developer MCP docs server and a markdown alternate on agents.ramp.com. Every element of the story is covered by first-party docs and live probes.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can point an agent at llms.txt or agent-oriented docs

citations.quote: PROBE llms.txt: HTTP 200 at https://docs.ramp.com/llms.txt # Ramp Developer API

fetch: /llms.txt (LLM index), /llms-guides.txt (guides index), /llms-guides/<slug>.txt (specific guide), /llms-api.txt (API reference), /llms-full.txt (combined docs), or /openapi/developer-api.json (OpenAPI spec)
GET https://docs.ramp.com/openapi/developer-api.json returns HTTP 200 — a parseable OpenAPI document titled "Ramp Developer API" (v1) with 174 documented paths
